**Job Summary**

The Executive Director is responsible for the overall operational and financial management of the Society of St. Vincent de Paul (SVdP) Sacramento Diocesan Council. This includes its thrift store and grant\-funded programs. The Executive Director reports directly to the President of the Council and the Board of Directors and ensures the organization's mission is fulfilled through effective programs, strategic planning, fundraising, and community engagement.

**Responsibilities**

Oversee daily operations of the thrift store and grant\-funded programs—including the Exodus Project, Disaster Relief, and Transition to Permanent Housing Solutions—to ensure sustainability and efficiency of the organization.

· Manage financial reporting, audits, and compliance with applicable local, state, and federal laws and regulations.

· Develop and manage an annual budget exceeding $3 million.

· Recruit, train, and supervise senior staff and program managers while fostering a positive, inclusive, and collaborative workplace for more than 70 employees.

· Lead fundraising initiatives, including annual campaigns, major gifts, grants, corporate partnerships, and special events.

· Partner closely with the Board of Directors to support board development, planning, and governance.

· Provide visionary management and strategic direction aligned with SVdP’s mission, values, and long\-term goals.

·Bachelor’s degree, or equivalent experience, in nonprofit management, retail, or a related field required.

· Master’s degree in nonprofit management, retail, or a related field preferred.

· Strong financial management skills, including budgeting and financial reporting, with solid working knowledge of QuickBooks.

· Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Outlook, Excel, and Word, is required; experience with nonprofit and retail management software is a plus.

· Minimum of three years, preferably five, in a senior nonprofit leadership role.

· Experience in retail operations, preferably in a thrift store setting.

· Proven success leading fundraising, grant writing, and donor relations efforts.

· Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.

· Demonstrated ability to work effectively with and support a Board of Directors.

· Commitment to ethical leadership and the organization’s mission.

· Must possess a valid California driver’s license.

This is a full\-time, exempt salaried position that requires on\-site, in\-person management at our thrift store location in Sacramento. Some evening and weekend work may be required. The role includes work in office, retail, and community settings.

To maximize commercial scalability and position the venture for venture capital backing, TeacherStudio360 will officially spin out into an independent corporation in early 2027\.

The platform’s core architecture and software development are 100% complete, live, and market\-ready (viewable at TeacherStudio360\.com). **About S.L.A.M. Trips**

S.L.A.M. (Students Learning About Missions) Trips is a program of Mending Wings, a Native\-led nonprofit youth organization located on the Yakama Nation in Washington State.

S.L.A.M. Trips welcomes youth, college students, families, churches and other groups to the Yakama Reservation for cross\-cultural service and learning experiences. Groups come as learners. Through service, relationships and cultural immersion, participants are invited to listen, learn and gain a deeper understanding of life and community on the Yakama Reservation.

Our approach challenges colonial models of short\-term missions and rebuilds the experience around Indigenous values, mutual respect and genuine relationships.

**Position Overview**

Mending Wings is seeking a dependable, organized and relationship\-focused person to lead the S.L.A.M. Trips program. The Director oversees all aspects of the program, including group recruitment, marketing, trip planning, budgeting, staff and intern supervision, community partnerships and hosting groups while they are on the Yakama Reservation.

Spring and summer are the program’s busiest seasons. During these months, the Director hosts visiting groups, supervises interns and volunteers, coordinates service projects and guides participants through meaningful cross\-cultural learning. During fall and winter, the work shifts toward recruiting, marketing, planning and preparing for the next season.

This position requires someone who can manage the practical details of a busy program while building genuine relationships with Yakama community members, visiting groups, interns, volunteers, Mending Wings staff and young people. Position Summary

The Director of Marketing and Communications will develop and execute the RILSH’s marketing, communications, and brand strategy in partnership with the CEO \& President, positioning Rhode Island as a leading destination for life science investment, talent, and company formation. The role pairs communications leadership — messaging, media relations, and public affairs — with hands\-on marketing operations: digital marketing, social media, and building the infrastructure and systems needed to generate, manage, and convert inbound and outbound leads into the RILSH pipeline.

The Director will coordinate closely with the communications teams at Rhode Island Commerce (“RI Commerce”), the Governor of Rhode Island’s Office, and other Rhode Island state agencies to align messaging and present a unified statewide voice for the life science sector. As part of a small management team, the Director will work directly with the CEO \& President to execute the organization’s strategy, coordinate signature events, and represent the RILSH to external audiences. This is a hands\-on, operator’s role that includes building the marketing and communications function — its systems, programs, and processes — largely from the ground up.

Essential Functions

Leadership \& Strategy

Partner with the CEO \& President to set marketing and communications strategy and translate it into execution.

Build the marketing and communications function — its structure, systems, and processes — and execute directly in a small, hands\-on team.

Manage agency partners, vendors, and contractors, with the ability to build and lead a small team over time.

Manage the marketing and communications budget.

Additional responsibilities as assigned and/or needed by the organization.

Communications \& Public Affairs

Develop and lead the RILSH’s overall communications strategy, including brand voice, messaging, media relations, press releases, talking points, executive communications, and thought leadership.

Manage issues and crisis communications, ensuring timely, accurate, and consistent responses.

Oversee core collateral and content — website copy, newsletters, annual reports, fact sheets, and executive presentations.

Own and execute the digital marketing strategy across web, email, search, and paid channels to build awareness and drive engagement.

Manage the organization’s social media presence (LinkedIn, X, and others), including content calendars, campaigns, community management, and analytics\-driven optimization.

Oversee the website — content, SEO, user experience, and performance — and manage web and creative vendor relationships.

Establish KPIs and reporting dashboards to measure reach, engagement, conversion, and return on investment across marketing channels.

Build out the marketing and business\-development infrastructure — CRM, marketing automation, and supporting systems and processes — to capture, track, nurture, and route inbound and outbound leads (companies, investors, site selectors, and partners).

Design and operate inbound lead\-capture pathways and outbound demand\-generation programs (targeted outreach, account\-based campaigns, and email sequences)and infrastructure to track, and manage the lead development and handoff process.

Partner with RI Commerce and business\-attraction stakeholders to align the RILSH lead pipeline with statewide business\-attraction efforts.

Coordinate and help manage RILSH events — roundtables, industry convenings, ribbon\-cuttings, conferences, and sponsorship activations — working with staff, vendors, and partners on planning, logistics, and follow\-up.

Represent and promote the RILSH at industry events, conferences, and community functions.

Stakeholder engagement \& interagency coordination: Job requires the ability to work effectively across internal and external stakeholders, including coordination with Rhode Island state agency and Governor’s Office communications teams.

Builder / operator: Job requires the ability to build marketing and communications systems, programs, and processes from the ground up and to execute them directly in a small, hands\-on team.

Initiative: Job requires a willingness to take on responsibilities and find ways over, around, or through barriers to success. A bias for action. A results\-oriented “doer.”

Qualifications

A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, public relations, business, or a related field; a master’s degree is a plus
